scale_005:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the financial data section of our board deck. Our banking/finance data lives in {{vendor}}, our startup banking platform. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) the reporting period/quarter for this board meeting, and (2) confirmation that you have configured credentials for {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard access.

Using your configured credentials, please:
1. Retrieve our current business bank/treasury account balances from {{vendor}}.
2. Pull the daily or monthly cash balance history for the quarter (and prior quarter for comparison) to show cash trend over time.
3. Pull the quarter's transactions (or a synced transaction export) to compile total spend, spend by category/vendor, and any notable large transactions worth flagging to the board.
4. If {{vendor}} supports categorized/synced accounting data (e.g., via its accounting software integration), use that categorization to speed up grouping expenses.

Organize the results into a clear summary suitable for a board slide: starting cash balance, ending cash balance, net burn/runway estimate (burn = change in cash over the period), top spend categories, and any anomalies or one-time items. Present this as a structured draft (table or bullet list) rather than raw transaction dumps, but keep the underlying transaction detail available in case someone asks follow-up questions.

Done looks like: a written summary with balances, cash trend, burn rate, and categorized spend for the period, plus a note of any data gaps (e.g., transactions still pending categorization) or access issues you hit. Report back the summary text, flag any numbers that look inconsistent or need finance-lead review, and stop for human sign-off before this data is treated as final for the board deck.

scale_005:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the revenue metrics section for our upcoming board deck. Our payment processing runs through {{vendor}}. Before starting, ask me for: (1) confirmation that your credentials for {{vendor}} are configured and ready to use, (2) the reporting period the board wants covered (e.g., last quarter, trailing 12 months), and (3) any specific revenue metrics the board typically expects (MRR, ARR, growth rate, churn, net revenue retention, etc.) beyond the standard set.

Once you have this, use {{vendor}}'s analytics/query interface (pre-built templates or SQL-style queries) to pull the following for the specified period:
- MRR and its month-over-month trend
- ARR
- Revenue growth rate
- Any available churn or retention metrics
- Payout and balance-transaction data, reconciled to underlying charges where possible
- A settlement-to-bank-deposit reconciliation summary, itemizing fees, refunds, and chargebacks if that level of detail is available

Compile the results into a clean summary table (metric, value, period-over-period comparison) plus a short reconciliation note confirming that reported revenue ties out to actual bank deposits (or flagging any discrepancies you found).

Done looks like: a draft revenue metrics section (table + brief narrative + reconciliation note) ready to drop into the board deck, along with a list of any data gaps or numbers you could not retrieve and why.

Report back with the compiled metrics, the reconciliation summary, and any flagged issues or missing data. Do not send or share this data outside of this task, and do not attempt to finalize or submit the board deck — just prepare the section for my review.

scale_005:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the financials section of our board deck. Please generate an accurate Profit & Loss statement from our {{vendor}} accounting system for the current board reporting period (ask me for the exact date range and comparison period if I haven't specified them, e.g. quarter-over-quarter or year-over-year).

Steps to take:
1. Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}} and pull the P&L report for the requested period, structured by standard categories (revenue, COGS, operating expenses, net income).
2. If useful for context, also pull the balance sheet and cash-flow statement for the same period, and the underlying general ledger or trial balance data if needed to verify totals.
3. Reconcile totals to confirm the P&L balances internally (e.g. gross margin, operating margin, net income all compute correctly from the line items).
4. Format the output into a clean summary table suitable for board deck insertion: line items, current period actuals, prior period comparison, and variance (% and $).
5. Note any anomalies, one-time items, or figures that look off and flag them for my review rather than silently adjusting them.

Done looks like: a verified P&L table (plus balance sheet/cash-flow if pulled) covering the requested period with period-over-period comparisons, ready to paste into the board deck, along with a short list of any flagged anomalies or data-quality concerns.

Report back with: the finalized P&L table, any supplementary statements pulled, the list of flagged items, and confirmation of which period(s) and comparison basis were used. Do not make any changes inside {{vendor}} itself — this is a read/export-only task.

scale_005:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the KPI and burn rate section of our board deck. Please ask me for anything you need that isn't already available, including: (1) where our financial data lives (e.g., a spreadsheet export, accounting software report, or bank statement data I can share), (2) the reporting period to cover (e.g., last quarter, trailing 12 months), (3) our current cash balance, (4) our defined KPI list (e.g., MRR/ARR, gross margin, CAC, LTV, churn, headcount, active users) or confirmation that you should use standard SaaS/startup KPIs if we don't have a custom list, and (5) prior period figures for comparison if available.

Once you have the data, calculate: monthly and annual burn rate (average monthly cash outflow over the period), runway (current cash balance divided by burn rate, expressed in months), month-over-month and period-over-period growth rates for revenue metrics, and any other KPIs from the list I give you (e.g., CAC, LTV, churn rate, gross margin, active users/customers). Show your calculation method and formulas clearly so I can verify them. Flag any data gaps, inconsistencies, or assumptions you had to make.

When done, report back a clean summary table with each KPI, its current value, prior period value, and percent change, plus a separate burn rate and runway summary (current burn, cash balance, runway in months). Note any metrics you could not calculate due to missing data, and tell me what additional data you'd need to complete them.

scale_005:n5.prompt:
You are helping me draft our board deck in Google Slides ahead of our upcoming board meeting. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in our shared drive or accessible via my configured credentials, specifically: (1) the target board meeting date, (2) our latest financial statements or a link to the finance tracker, (3) current key metrics (revenue, growth, burn, runway, churn, or whatever we track), (4) a summary of recent product updates or a changelog, (5) the current hiring plan/headcount doc, and (6) the specific asks or decisions we want the board to weigh in on.

Once you have these inputs, create a new Google Slides presentation titled with our company name, 'Board Deck', and the meeting date. Structure it with these sections as separate slides: Cover/Agenda, Financial Summary, Key Metrics, Product Updates, Hiring Plan, Asks/Discussion Items, and Appendix (for supporting detail). Populate each section using the data and documents I provide, formatting numbers into clear tables or simple charts where useful, and keeping bullet points concise and board-appropriate. Reuse our standard deck formatting/branding if a prior board deck exists in the drive that you can reference as a template.

When done, share the Google Slides link with me and provide a brief summary listing: what data source was used for each section, any gaps where I still need to supply information, and any assumptions you made while drafting. Do not send, present, or share this deck with the board or any external party — this remains a step for me to review and finalize before distribution.

scale_005:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the 'Strategy and Asks' section of my board deck. This section requires my personal strategic input, so your job is to draft a clean, well-organized slide structure and placeholder content that I can review and finalize — not to invent the actual strategy or asks yourself.

First, ask me for any of the following if not already provided: my company name, the board meeting date, the deck platform I use (Google Slides or PowerPoint), and access to the existing board deck file or template if one exists. Also ask me to supply, in bullet form: (1) my top 2-4 strategic priorities for the next quarter/year, (2) any pivots or changes in direction, (3) specific asks for the board (e.g., fundraising support, intros, hiring help, approvals needed), and (4) any risks or challenges I want flagged.

Once I provide that raw content, organize it into a polished slide outline: a 'Strategic Priorities' slide, a 'Key Asks from the Board' slide (with each ask clearly stated and what response/action I need), and optionally a 'Risks & Open Questions' slide. Use concise, board-ready language, format consistently with the rest of the deck, and insert these slides into the existing deck file in the correct position (typically after product updates and before closing).

Do not add strategic claims, financial projections, or asks that I have not explicitly given you — only format and organize what I provide. Once the slides are drafted and inserted, share the current draft with me for review and stop for human sign-off before the deck is considered final or shared with the board.

scale_005:n7.prompt:
You are helping me publish our compiled board meeting deck into our {{vendor}} board room workspace, using {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard with my configured credentials. Before starting, ask me for anything you need: (1) the finalized board deck content (financials, metrics, product updates, hiring plan, and asks — either as a file, doc link, or pasted text), (2) the {{vendor}} workspace/team and the specific parent page or 'board room' section where this should live, and (3) any naming convention or template structure I want followed (e.g., page title format, section headers).

Once you have the content and destination, do the following:
1. Organize the deck content into a clean, structured page: sections for Financials, Metrics, Product Updates, Hiring Plan, and Asks, formatted with headers, tables, or bullet lists as appropriate for {{vendor}}.
2. Prepare the new page as a draft in the correct location within {{vendor}}, using its API or dashboard — do not create/publish it live yet.
3. Produce a summary showing: the proposed page title, its location in the workspace hierarchy, and the full formatted content for each section.
4. Flag any missing or unclear inputs (e.g., incomplete metrics, missing hiring numbers) rather than guessing.

Because this step requires explicit human approval before changes are applied, do not create, publish, or share the page in {{vendor}} yet. Present the complete draft and structure to me for review and stop for human sign-off. Once I confirm, I will tell you to proceed with publishing.

Report back with: the prepared page draft (title, hierarchy location, full content by section), any open questions or missing data, and a clear note that the page is staged and awaiting my approval before it goes live.

scale_005:n8.prompt:
You are helping me send the finalized board deck to our board members via Gmail. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for anything you don't already have: the board deck file or link, the list of board member email addresses, the subject line I want to use, and any key talking points or a summary I want included in the email body (financial highlights, metrics, product updates, hiring plan, and specific asks for the board).
2. Draft a professional email addressed to the board members that briefly summarizes the deck's key sections (financials, metrics, product updates, hiring plan, asks) and clearly states any decisions or feedback needed from the board before the meeting.
3. Attach or link the board deck in the draft, using your configured credentials to access Gmail.
4. Prepare the draft as a Gmail draft (not sent) addressed to all board members, with subject line and body fully filled in, ready for final review.
5. Provide me a checklist showing: recipients included, subject line, summary of body content, and confirmation the deck is attached/linked correctly.
6. Do not send the email. Because sending requires my explicit approval, you must stop for human sign-off once the draft is fully prepared and reviewed by me.

When done, report back with: the Gmail draft link or identifier, the final recipient list, the subject line, a copy of the email body text, and confirmation that the deck attachment/link is correct. Explicitly note that the email is staged as a draft awaiting my approval and has not been sent.
